clue.text: Exercises, keeping to central compound

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the exercises letters hold the rest inside them

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
main means chief or central, as in the main road

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor urges people to stick to core movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like part of the gym jargon (a compound exercise) but is the definition: a chemical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chemical produced by decaying protein, a nitrogen-bearing organic substance.

clue.text: Challenge mission no-one's backing

parts.note: a quest is a mission or expedition

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: NO plus one as the Roman-numeral-like I

explanation.surface: Nobody supports a demanding assignment, so it gets disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'no-one's' splits into NO and one (I) for the reversal signalled by 'backing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something into doubt is to challenge it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary people's fish topped and tailed

indicators.note: topping and tailing removes the first and last letters, like trimming vegetables

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A fish is prepared for ordinary people by cutting off its head and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' strips P and E from PLAICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lay, belonging to laypeople rather than the clergy, adjective for ordinary folk.

clue.text: New Hampshire son's art mounted

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh or remade version, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as SON, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A boy from New Hampshire has a talent for something on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the US state's name but is the anagram signal on HAMPSHIRE plus SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill at riding is the art practised when mounted on a horse.

clue.text: Bar in base dispensed with

indicators.note: in places the bar's letters inside the base's letters

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of gravel
an inn is a bar or pub

explanation.surface: A drinks bar at a military base has been closed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing something in the rubbish bin means discarding or getting rid of it.

clue.text: Alert wife's fled owing rent when sacked

indicators.note: sacked suggests something ransacked or plundered and left in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
fled means has gone away, so the wife's letter leaves the word owing

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife, with 's as has
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant is warned that his wife has left him, owing rent after he lost his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fled' removes W from OWING, leaving OING; 'sacked' rearranges OING plus RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone's ringing sound is an alert that a call is arriving.

clue.text: Shred letter introducing street fighter in revolution

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the letter takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: vee is the spelt-out name of the letter V

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A scrap of writing introduces a street fighter in a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' stands for a letter's spelt-out name, VEE; GI is the usual crossword soldier, turned by 'in revolution'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny remaining trace of something, a shred of evidence, is a synonym.

clue.text: Chief's pledge to restrict a rival's borders

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the pledge closes round the rest

parts.note: your word is your pledge or promise

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outside letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A leader makes a promise to keep a rival within bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' acts on the bare word rival, the 's being a link; 'to restrict' makes the pledge the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A military commander ruling a region is a chief, a synonym.

clue.text: Corrupt, deposing leader after petition's produced

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word following the petition's letters

parts.note: to beg is to petition or plead

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: rotten means corrupt

explanation.surface: Corruption, after its ringleader is removed, has led to a formal petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing leader' cuts the first letter; 'petition's produced' reads as petition has produced, so the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical word for fathered or generated, so a fair synonym for produced.

clue.text: American bishop stops porter working

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the bishop's letter goes inside the beer

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An American bishop prevents a hotel porter from doing his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' reads as a doorman but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in working order is fit for use, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Elite philosopher's restricting time, oddly afraid to take the lead

indicators.note: to take the lead puts these letters at the front of the answer
oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word
restricting means confining, so the philosopher's adjective holds the time letter

parts.note: Socratic means belonging to Socrates the philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker's ideas about time were too timid to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' works on afraid, and 'to take the lead' sends that pick to the front; the philosopher's adjective is the one from Socrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite is used as an adjective for the upper class, the nobility's sort.

clue.text: Gents possibly retiring after duck here?

definitions.text: Gents possibly retiring after duck here?

indicators.note: after places the turned word following the duck's letter

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nothing, an O

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a gents is a men's toilet, an example of a lav

explanation.surface: Men head to the toilet after a batting failure at a cricket venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London Test-cricket ground; in cricket a duck is a score of nought, after which the batsman retires to the pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous cricket ground in London where gentlemen batsmen might walk off after a duck.

clue.text: Clergyman from drama finally axed in series

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed drama inside the series

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things

indicators.note: finally axed means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A clergyman is cut from a drama series in the final episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; 'finally axed' trims the drama word before 'in' places it inside the series.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric attached to a regiment, hospital or college is a clergyman.

clue.text: Plucked rose?

parts.note: a garden flower that has been picked and collected into a bunch, the question mark flagging the whimsical reading

explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that have been picked are collected, so a plucked bloom has been brought in.

clue.text: Drawing the author's appended to pamphlet

indicators.note: appended to means added on the end, so these letters follow the pamphlet

parts.note: a tract is a pamphlet
the author is I, the setter, and 's stands for have, giving I've

explanation.surface: A drawing by the writer is attached to a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes pulling power, as a traction engine draws a load.

clue.text: Communities headed by male preferring current to old schemes

indicators.note: headed by puts the altered word in front of the communities
current is I in physics and old is O, so I takes the place of O

parts.note: macho means very masculine, a male type
nations are communities of people

explanation.surface: Communities led by a man who prefers modern ways to old ones draw up plans.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the symbol for electric current; O for old; MACHO becomes MACHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty plots and intrigues are schemes, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Unbecoming short blue clothing RAF abandoned

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the shortened colour surrounds the other letters
short means missing its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: indigo is a shade of blue

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Short blue uniforms are no longer worn by the Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' is the anagram signal on the air force's initials, and 'clothing' makes the shortened colour the container; the phrase is short for Latin infra dignitatem.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for beneath one's dignity, so behaviour that is unseemly or undignified.

clue.text: Royal aide in palace ultimately doubt, king admitted

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of the word
admitted means let in, so the doubt takes the king's letter inside

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: An official in the palace finally raises a question once the king lets him in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E from PALACE; 'admitted' puts R inside QUERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the royal household who attends the monarch is a personal assistant.

clue.text: Worried about fuelling row? Shut up!

indicators.note: fuelling means feeding into, so the letters go inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a row or racket

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ate as in what's eating you, worried

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about stoking an argument is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' is past tense of eat in the sense 'what's eating you'; 'about' turns it, 'fuelling' puts it in the row. 'Shut up' is the verb, to lock away.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone up in a cell is to confine or hold them.

clue.text: Powerful superior going off

definitions.meaning: elevated in rank, as in a lofty office
of meat or game, starting to rot and smell

explanation.definitionFit: Strong winds, lofty rank and gamey meat all use this one adjective for elevated or ripe.

clue.text: Plant pile the two of us had reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.words: pile the two of us had
parts.note: nap is the pile on a fabric, and we'd is a contraction of we had

explanation.surface: A gardener tells of a heap of cuttings two people had collected.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP (pile) + WE'D (the two of us had) said together give a word spelt with a silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple-flowered thistle-like meadow wildflower, so a type of plant.

clue.text: People — twenty — obtain revenge

parts.note: to people a place is to settle it, the verb sense
a score is twenty

explanation.surface: Twenty people take vengeance together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun but is the verb, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means paying someone back for an old wrong, taking revenge.

clue.text: Nobbled by vicar full of new energy

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the jumbled letters hold the new letter
nobbled means tampered with, so the letters are interfered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A racehorse was nobbled by an energetic vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobbled' rearranges BY VICAR into VIBRACY; 'full of' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and vigour are a kind of energy, a noun synonym.

clue.text: A cat's tail spotted in whimsical etching

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside, so the tail letter sits within the word

parts.note: quaint means oddly old-fashioned, whimsical

indicators.note: tail means the final letter

explanation.surface: A cat's tail can be seen in a fanciful engraving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' takes T from CAT; 'spotted in' puts it inside QUAINT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a print made by an acid-etching process giving tonal washes.

clue.text: After overthrow of queen, ambassador's lower in status

indicators.note: after places the ambassador's letters following the turned queen
overthrow means turning upside down, so the queen's letters are reversed

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, queen
a legate is an envoy or ambassador

explanation.surface: After the queen is toppled, the ambassador loses rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ambassador's' is ambassador is, a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote someone or something to a lower rank or division.

clue.text: Disruptive noise from son playing with band

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is a band, as in a wedding band

explanation.surface: A boy is making a racket playing with his band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals an anagram, not ON; 'from' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud breathing while asleep is a disturbing sound in a shared bedroom.

clue.text: God on a cross showing where his heart lies?

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A god shown on a cross reveals his innermost feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where his heart lies' sounds like his true loyalty, but it is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest cavity houses the heart and lungs, so it is literally where the heart is.

clue.text: Prayer leader's friend from Paris turned up before Mass

indicators.note: before puts the turned friend ahead of the mass letter
turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A Parisian friend shows up before attending Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who leads congregational worship in a mosque is a Muslim prayer leader.
